requirements.requirement: On node1, add at least 512 MB of disk-backed swap that is active and preferred over existing swap.
requirements.summary: A fully allocated 512 MiB /swapfile was created and activated. Direct observations show it active at priority 100 while the existing /dev/vda3 swap remains active at priority -2.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the added swap is active at boot.
requirements.summary: The fstab entry was validated and successfully reactivated before restart. A bounded restart changed the boot identity, after which /swapfile was directly observed active through the generated swap unit at priority 100, with the system healthy.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after observations consistently show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The solution uses the platform's working native swap and systemd/fstab facilities, with no package changes observed.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has an active, fully allocated 512 MiB disk-backed swapfile preferred over the existing swap, and direct restart evidence proves boot persistence and healthy recovery. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities; the OS release and kernel remained unchanged.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating and activating /swapfile and adding its fstab entry directly implemented the task; the temporary swapoff/reactivation was a bounded persistence test; daemon reload and restart established boot behavior; and the temporary reboot log was removed. Post-execution evidence shows no failed services, unexpected socket exposure, package damage, or abandoned temporary file. The initial failed swapon query and restart-time connection failures provide no evidence of unwanted mutation.
